assumptions: Focus on user flow over internal systems
Assume stories should be independently testable
Assume each story delivers user value
Assume technical infrastructure stories are implicit
Drill down where architectural uncertainty is high – unknown integration patterns, new technology, or unclear system boundaries require deeper exploration
Drill down where business complexity is significant – complex business rules, regulatory requirements, or domain logic that needs clarification
Drill down where uniqueness creates risk – novel approaches, first-of-kind features, or untested patterns benefit from detailed shaping
Drill down where integration complexity exists – multiple systems, data dependencies, or coordination challenges need detailed mapping
Drill down where user behavior is highly variable – diverse user needs, multiple personas, or inconsistent workflows require deeper understanding
Skip deep drill-down where patterns are well-established – standard CRUD operations, familiar workflows, or proven integration patterns can stay high-level
Focus on core domain over supporting domains
Identify overall domain concepts and relationships before detailed modeling
Use ubiquitous language from domain sources
Model domain concepts, not technical implementation
Separate domain logic from infrastructure concerns, where they are mentioned

answers.user_types: Game Master (GM) - primary user running RPG sessions using Foundry VTT
answers.user_goals: Group minions into mobs that act together, control entire mob with single action, select combat strategies (attack strongest, attack weakest, defend leader, attack most damaged), manage minion grouping (create, edit, spawn from templates)
answers.first_action: Create a mob by grouping existing minion tokens
answers.problems_eliminated: Eliminates repetitive clicking of individual minion tokens to perform actions
answers.struggles: During combat/action sequences when controlling many minions, requiring repeated manual token selection and action execution
answers.value_drivers: Efficiency (faster combat), ease of use (reduced clicks), tactical depth (strategy selection), smoother game flow
answers.outcomes: Faster minion management, easier combat control, more engaging game sessions with less repetitive work
answers.user_journey: 1. Identify minions to group 2. Create/group them into a mob 3. Select a mob strategy 4. Click one mob token 5. All minions in the mob perform the same action per the selected strategy
answers.journey_stages: Mob creation/grouping (select tokens -> create mob), Strategy selection (choose attack/defend strategy), Action execution (click token -> all minions act), Mob management (edit, spawn from templates, choose targets)
answers.frustration_points: At the action execution stage - having to repeatedly click each minion token to perform the same action
answers.delight_moments: When clicking one token makes an entire mob act together, and when strategy selection adds tactical depth to combat
answers.pain_points: Time-consuming individual token management, lack of unified control for grouped minions, absence of strategy-based automation
answers.system_integrations: Foundry VTT system: actors, tokens, combat system, targeting, movement/ranging, area attacks, templates, actor spawning mechanisms
answers.integration_points: Token selection/grouping -> mob entity creation, Strategy selection -> target determination logic, Target selection -> integration with Foundry targeting, Action execution -> Foundry combat system, Movement/ranging -> Foundry movement/range rules, Area attacks -> Foundry area/template system
answers.business_domain: Game session management within a virtual tabletop RPG system, specifically minion/mob combat management
answers.core_concepts: Minion (individual combatant token), Mob (collection of minions acting as unit), Strategy (decision rules for mob behavior), Token (visual representation in Foundry VTT), Actor (underlying game entity), Target (combat target selection), Action (combat action performed by mob)
answers.sub_domains: Mob management (create, edit, group, spawn from templates), Strategy selection (choose combat strategy), Target selection (select targets based on strategy), Action execution (perform actions on selected targets), Movement/ranging (handle range and movement requirements)
answers.domain_boundaries: Mob management vs Foundry core token/actor system, Strategy logic vs Foundry combat system, Target selection vs Foundry targeting UI/system, Action execution vs Foundry action/combat resolution
answers.domain_events: Mob created, Minions grouped into mob, Strategy selected, Target chosen (by strategy), Mob action executed, All minions in mob perform action, Mob edited, Mob spawned from template
answers.business_rules: A mob is a collection of minions that act together, One click on any mob token triggers actions for all minions in the mob, Strategy determines target selection (strongest, weakest, most damaged, defend leader), Must work within Foundry VTT system architecture, Range/movement rules apply (characters may need to move to target), Area attacks are supported, Fleeing/flee mechanics exist (not primary focus)
answers.domain_language: Minions, mobs, tokens, actors (Foundry terminology), Strategies: attack strongest, attack weakest, defend leader, attack most damaged, Grouping, spawning, templates, targeting, Range, movement, area attacks, fleeing, Game Master (GM), combat, actions
